- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.8) and forecast is below recent high, adjust upward by 1–2% to capture momentum.
- When sentiment is negative (≤ 0.2) and forecast is above recent low, adjust downward by 1–2% to avoid overcorrection.
- Avoid forecasting sharp spikes: if last 3–5 days show rapid upward movement, cap forecast rise to 10–15% max to prevent overshoot.
- If sentiment is volatile (alternating high/low), apply mean reversion: forecast should not deviate more than 1.5σ from 14-day moving average.
- For 30-day horizon, if true outcome exceeds forecast by >5% for 3+ consecutive days, reduce next forecast by 1–3% to avoid lagged overestimation.
- If sentiment history shows recent reversal (e.g., from +0.8 to -0.3), reduce forecast slope by 20–40% for next 5 days to reflect sentiment shift.
